confidence_notes: Three web searches were used: one for the RBA rate and two for Cluj-Napoca food and drink prices. They found aggregated figures from MyLifeElsewhere (2026) and Expatistan, plus a 2026 Romania guide from Freenance. The search summaries put an inexpensive meal with a drink at about RON 50 (about USD 11.50), a pint of local beer at about RON 15 (about USD 3.45), and a cappuccino at about RON 13-22, mostly about RON 15. They put cocktails at about RON 23 in the Expatistan figure and RON 22-38 in the 2026 guide. The cappuccino estimate uses the main figure of about RON 15, so it is fairly solid. The cocktail price is a midpoint of the RON 22-38 range, at about RON 34 (about USD 7.75). No price for a glass of wine was found, only bottle prices of about RON 35-43. The wine estimate of about RON 22 is based on the bottle prices and the usual wine-to-beer price ratio, so it is less certain. No aggregated three-course mid-range meal figure was found. That anchor is a model estimate of about RON 260 for two, consistent with the RON 98 pub dinner for two and the RON 54 business lunch on Expatistan. All accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge and were not checked against live listings or search results. July demand in Cluj is pushed up by festivals and the city has limited hostel stock, so these values are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Cluj-Napoca is one of Romania's most expensive cities, alongside Bucharest, and prices run about 20% above the Romanian average. Food and drink prices are similar to Bucharest and Timisoara and a bit below Budapest. Accommodation is estimated by comparison with other secondary Central and Eastern European cities with summer festival demand, such as Brasov, Sibiu and Debrecen.
